newsitem.title: USA: U.S. women soldiers say raped at base in Germany.
newsitem.headline: U.S. women soldiers say raped at base in Germany.

text.p: The U.S. Army, already hit by sexual scandal at home, is investigating allegations by 11 women soldiers that they were harassed or raped by male instructors at a base in Germany, the Army said on Wednesday.

A statement released by the Army's personnel training centre at Darmstadt said complaints by some of the women also included forcible sodomy and that three male instructors had been relieved of duty pending outcome of the investigation.

No formal charges were filed, but two of the three suspects were confined last week based on reports that they contacted one alleged victim in an attempt to influence her testimony, according to the statement.

"The remaining suspect has been ordered by his chain of command not to contact any victim or witness," it said, adding that Army Criminal Investigative Division personnel questioned about 70 people in the investigation.

The Army, meanwhile, continued to investigate a growing sexual harassment scandal at training bases in the United States in which a number of male drill sergeants were charged with wrongdoing ranging from harassment to rape and sodomy of young women recruits.
On Monday, the Army also suspended from duty in Washington the service's top enlisted man pending resolution of sexual harassment allegations against him by a retired woman soldier.
Army officials, who asked not to be identified, said they were also looking into harassment allegations by two other servicewomen against Army Sgt. Maj. Gene McKinney. They declined to give details.

Although the Army's presence in Germany and elsewhere in Europe shrank after the Cold War ended, the U.S. military still maintains a force of nearly 100,000 soldiers, sailors and Air Force personnel in the European theatre.

The Army maintains an Individual Training Centre (ITC) at Darmstadt which is attended by all soldiers arriving for duty with the base support battalion and other units in the immediate area. Those soldiers have already undergone basic training in the United States.

The unofficial U.S. military newspaper European Stars and Stripes reported on Wednesday that two of the male instructors involved in the case had been confined to the Mannheim Correctional Facility since last Saturday.
"Allegations under investigation include rape, forcible sodomy, indecent assault and cruelty and maltreatment of a subordinate," according to the statement released in Darmstadt.
"The incidents will be investigated fully and the command will take the appropriate judicial, non-judicial or administrative actions as appropriate in each case," it said.
The statement said that the investigation grew out of a complaint made in November by a woman soldier assigned to a signal brigade. She filed an official complaint in December.
